component.name: InfiniteNote
component.summary: Local-first OneNote-style notebook with an infinite canvas

description.p: InfiniteNote is an open-source OneNote-style notebook for Linux and Android: organize notes in a Notebook → Section → Page hierarchy and write on an infinite canvas where you can draw and type anywhere. Everything is stored locally (IndexedDB) and the app works offline.

ul.li: Infinite canvas (Excalidraw): draw, type, move and resize anything
Import images, text, Markdown, PDF printouts, Word documents, .excalidraw scenes and OneNote exports (.html and .mht single-file pages with embedded images)
Export PNG, SVG, paginated A4 PDF, .excalidraw scenes and full notebook backups
Cross-page full-text search, page tags with a filter view, quick capture with a pinned Today page
Per-page paper styles: plain, ruled and grid
Soft-delete trash with restore, dark mode, offline-first PWA
File-based sync to a local folder or ZIP with page-granular merge and conflict copies

Mobile layout with the navigation drawer

description.p: Export a whole notebook as one paginated PDF (OneNote's "Export notes as a PDF — Notebook"): the notebook menu gains "Export as PDF" in A4 portrait/landscape — every alive section opens on a divider sheet (its name, page count and section color, plus the parent group name when nested), then its alive pages flow on fresh sheets through the shared print engine; one document, a global sheet counter, empty sections keep their divider.

Export a whole section as one paginated PDF (OneNote's "Export notes as a PDF — Section"): the section menu gains "Export as PDF" in A4 portrait/landscape — every alive page of the section flows into one document in sidebar order, pages without ink keep their footer on a blank sheet, and the print engine it shares with the per-page export is now a data-driven core.

Section groups arrive (OneNote's Section Groups): "New section group" on the notebook and section menus lands a folder-glyph group that keeps related sections together and holds no pages of its own; groups nest at the notebook top level or under other groups, and sections, pages, trash, sync and backup all behave around them.

Sections move (sub-sections phase 2): drag a section onto another to nest it or onto a notebook for a cross-notebook top-level move, with a Move-to dialog as the keyboard path; invalid targets never accept. Ink to shape arrives (OneNote's Ink to Shape): drawn shapes become perfect geometry in one undo step, while strokes that do not look like a shape stay ink.

Sub-sections arrive (OneNote's section groups / Joplin's sub-notebooks): a section can contain child sections — any section holds pages AND child sections at once, subtree trash/restore/purge cascades, and nesting that survives backups and sync. Section colors arrive too (OneNote's "Section Color"): every section carries its own color with notebook inheritance, recolored from the section menu's Color submenu.

Checklists arrive: every page can carry OneNote-style To Do items — type a line, right-click it and Add To Do tag, then Toggle checked as you complete items; the checked state is the text itself, so it survives reload, sync, backups and search untouched. An Import-menu Checklist item starter drops a bare checkbox line.

OneNote everyday-parity release: tables on pages (Insert > Table), general file attachments (Insert > File Attachment), and custom page templates (save a page as a reusable template, create pages from a picker).

Hardening and community release: OS share capture into Quick Notes (Web Share Target), security hardening (strict desktop CSP, web security headers, least-privilege CI, audited lockfiles), community health docs, and CI/release automation practices adopted from major open-source repos.
Hardening and measurement release: independent desktop-artifact verification, and the WebGPU handwriting investigation concluded with the measured decision to stay on the WASM engine.
Handwriting made fully usable end to end — written, found (handwriting search), and converted to text — entirely on-device.
Handwriting-recognition research write-up: the decision basis for on-device HTR work (docs/handwriting-research.md).
Desktop fix: the AppImage is rebuilt against the ubuntu-22.04 glibc 2.35 floor so it launches on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 and Mint 22; README and troubleshooting rework.
Page version history, on-device OCR for images (English and German), and OneNote-style PDF file chips that keep the original file.
Patch release: fresh element ids on every shape insert (#65 follow-up).
OneNote-style shape library (toolbar with blocks, arrow variants, elbow connectors and sticky notes) and a bundled-asset Android TWA that renders offline on first run (F-Droid compliance).
Focused English-only interface: the v1.7 i18n layer (next-intl, catalogs, language toggle) removed; CJK note content remains fully supported.
Audio blocks: import audio files or record straight into the page — clips play as on-canvas players and persist locally; import-test hardening wave.
Internationalization (English + 简体中文) and polish: a six-accent themes gallery over light/dark, and the F-Droid build recipe with validation tooling.

Distribution release: the desktop app is packaged for Linux (Tauri shell with deb/rpm/AppImage artifacts attached to GitHub releases, a Flatpak manifest, and an Android Trusted Web Activity scaffold with Digital Asset Links tooling).
File-based sync, phase 1: export notebooks to a sync folder or merge from one (File System Access or ZIP), with page-granular three-way merge, conflict copies and purge tombstones.
Sidebar multi-select with bulk move/delete, an in-app keyboard shortcut cheatsheet, and a sync & collaboration research write-up.
Page tags with a tag filter view, quick capture (Quick note button + Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+N) with a pinned Today daily page, and print-friendly paginated A4 PDF export.
